Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
Comments: International internet bandwidth per internet user reported <5 kbps/user (very low). [GlobalEconomy/ITU](https://www.theglobaleconomy.com/Burkina-Faso/Internet_bandwidth/)
revision_notes: Confirmed via TheGlobalEconomy.com, which cites ITU World Telecommunication Indicators data. The most recent published figure for Burkina Faso is 3.15 kbit/s per internet user (2015), within the ITU data series covering 2012-2015. No fresher country-specific figure could be located via ITU DataHub (interactive tool not accessible for direct data extraction) or other sources on a limited check; 3.15 kbit/s remains well under the 5 kbit/s threshold for Value Code 1.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso's international internet bandwidth per internet user stands at approximately 3.15 kilobits per second, according to ITU World Telecommunication Indicators data (most recent available figure, 2015), placing the country in the 'very low' category (<5 kbit/s per user) that is typical of landlocked Sahelian states reliant on cross-border terrestrial fibre links.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
Comments: Urban electricity access ~62.6% vs rural ~2% (~60pp gap; very high inequality). [Trading Economics (World Bank urban)](https://tradingeconomics.com/burkina-faso/access-to-electricity-urban-percent-of-urban-population-wb-data.html) [World Bank rural](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS?locations=BF)
revision_notes: Confirmed by fetching both cited World Bank SDG7/ESMAP-sourced pages. Rural electricity access in Burkina Faso is 2.0% (2023, World Bank EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS) and urban access is 62.6% (2023, World Bank EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS via Trading Economics), giving a gap of 60.6 percentage points. This falls just within the >60pp band, supporting Value Code 1.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso shows a very large urban-rural electrification gap: 2023 World Bank SDG7 data record urban electricity access at 62.6% of the urban population against just 2.0% in rural areas, a gap of roughly 61 percentage points, reflecting heavy concentration of grid infrastructure in Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso and other main towns.
